bib.title: Making Pre-trained Language Models Better Few-shot Learners
bib.venue: ACL-IJCNLP 2021 (59th Annual Meeting of the ACL and 11th IJCNLP), pages 3816-3830

question: How can a moderately sized masked language model be fine-tuned well from only a few annotated examples per class?
hypothesis: Casting the task as masked-LM prompting (with automatically searched prompts) and adding sampled in-context demonstrations will beat standard fine-tuning in the few-shot setting.
contributions: Prompt-based fine-tuning with a pipeline for automatic prompt generation (label-word search, T5 template generation)
A refined strategy for dynamically and selectively incorporating demonstrations into each context
A systematic few-shot evaluation over 15 tasks (classification and regression) with 5 resampled splits and a few-shot-sized dev set

method.summary: LM-BFF fine-tunes RoBERTa-large as a masked LM on a template with a [MASK] filled by label words, reusing pretrained output embeddings (no new head). Templates are generated by T5-3B beam search and label words by a pruned brute-force search, both chosen on a dev set the same size as the training set. Optionally one demonstration per class, chosen among the top 50% most similar by SBERT, is concatenated to the input.
method.task: few-shot text classification and regression (8 single-sentence and 7 sentence-pair English tasks)

datasets.name: SST-2, SST-5, MR, CR, MPQA, Subj, TREC, CoLA, MNLI, SNLI, QNLI, RTE, MRPC, QQP, STS-B
datasets.size: K=16 examples per class for train and a dev set of equal size (K x |Y|); full sizes in Table B.1 (e.g. SST-2 6,920 train / 872 test; SNLI 549,367 / 9,842; STS-B 5,749 / 1,500)
datasets.source: GLUE, SNLI and others; for GLUE/SNLI the original dev sets are used for testing (following Zhang et al., 2021); for MR, CR, MPQA, Subj 2,000 random examples are held out as test; SST-5 and TREC use official test sets
datasets.preprocessing: Templates add a space before a sentence not at the start; first letter lowercased when concatenated to a prefix; trailing character dropped when punctuation is appended; label words get a leading space (' great'). STS-B regression partitioned into two classes at the median for sampling.

other.note: context 512 stated as typical for RoBERTa-style small LMs; a standard classification head adds 2,048 parameters for binary tasks (footnote/Sec 4)

other.role_note: Appendix D comparison, 4 tasks, manual prompts

other.use: template generation by beam search, width e.g. 100; largest public one that fits on one GPU

other.note: trained on SNLI and MNLI, acknowledged in Sec 7.3

training.objective: classification: cross-entropy over softmax of [MASK] logits restricted to label words (Eq 1); regression: KL divergence between inferred p(yu|x) and (y-vl)/(vu-vl) (Eq 2)
training.lr: grid {1e-5, 2e-5, 5e-5}, chosen per split on Ddev; fixed 1e-5 for automatic prompt search trials
training.batch_size: grid {2, 4, 8}, chosen per split on Ddev; fixed 8 for automatic prompt search trials
training.steps: 1,000 steps per trial, validated every 100 steps, best checkpoint kept
training.regularisation: early stopping via best-checkpoint selection on Ddev
training.hardware: single GPU (type not stated); T5-3B described as the largest that fits on a single GPU
training.seeds: 5 random (Dtrain, Ddev) splits; hyper-parameters swept per split

other.no_ddev_baseline: Schick and Schutze setting: batch size 16, lr 1e-5, 250 steps (Appendix A)
other.demonstrations: 16 demonstration sets sampled per input at train and test; predicted log probabilities averaged over sets; more samples gave no substantial gain

inference.decoding: argmax over label-word probabilities at [MASK]; with demonstrations, average of log-probs over 16 sampled demonstration sets
inference.samples: 5 splits; 16 demonstration sets per input when demonstrations are used
inference.prompting: manual templates (Table 1) or auto templates; demonstrations: one random example per class from the top r=50% most SBERT-similar training examples, concatenated after the input template
inference.retrieval: SBERT cosine similarity between query and class-c training sentences (sentence pairs concatenated, raw text without templates); sample from top r = 50% per class

parameters.label_word_topk_k: 100 for all tasks except SST-5 (30) and TREC (1000, then re-ranked by nearest neighbours of manual label words, top 30 per class)
parameters.label_word_n: 100 assignments fine-tuned and re-ranked on Ddev

baselines: "GPT-3" in-context learning with RoBERTa-large (32 random demonstrations, no updates)
Standard fine-tuning on full training set
eval.protocol: Mean (std) over 5 random Dtrain/Ddev splits; hyper-parameters swept per split and selected on that split's Ddev (size equal to Dtrain). SST-2 and SNLI used for pilot experiments and development. No significance tests stated.

availability.data: public benchmark datasets; splits not stated as released

prompts.purpose: Manual templates and label words, all tasks
prompts.text: SST-2/MR/CR/SST-5: '<S1> It was [MASK] .' (great/terrible; SST-5 great/good/okay/bad/terrible); Subj/CoLA: '<S1> This is [MASK] .' (subjective/objective; correct/incorrect); TREC: '[MASK] : <S1>' (Expression/Entity/Description/Human/Location/Number); MNLI/SNLI/QNLI/RTE: '<S1> ? [MASK] , <S2>' (Yes/Maybe/No; Yes/No); MRPC/QQP/STS-B: '<S1> [MASK] , <S2>' (Yes/No)

prompts.purpose: Top-3 automatic templates and label words per task
prompts.text: see Table E.1, e.g. SST-2 '<S1> A [MASK] one .' with irresistible/pathetic

evidence.quote: only sample from the top r = 50% instances for each class to use as demonstrations

results.claim: The combined method (auto templates plus sampled demonstrations) gains up to 30 points on SNLI over standard fine-tuning and 11 points on average.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16 per class, 15 tasks, mean over 5 splits, Table 3 (auto + demonstrations vs Fine-tuning)
results.quote: achieves a 30% gain on SNLI compared to standard ﬁne-tuning, and 11% gain on average.
results.note: Table 3 SNLI auto+demos 77.5 vs fine-tuning 48.4 (29.1 points) and manual+demos 79.7 vs 48.4 (31.3); 30% is the paper's rounded figure

results.claim: Label-word choice moves SST-2 accuracy: great/terrible 92.7, swapped terrible/great 83.2 (standard fine-tuning is 81.4).
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16, template '<S1> It was [MASK] .', mean over 5 splits; std 0.9 vs 6.9
results.table: Table 2, SST-2 rows great/terrible 92.7 (0.9) and terrible/great 83.2 (6.9); Fine-tuning 81.4 (3.8)

results.claim: Template wording and sentence order change SNLI accuracy by more than 10 points with the same label words.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16, label words Yes/Maybe/No; '<S1> ? [MASK] , <S2>' 77.2 vs swapped '<S2> ? [MASK] , <S1>' 62.9; [MASK] at the end 65.8; permuted label words Maybe/No/Yes 60.6
results.quote: if we put [MASK] at the end, or swap sentence order, we observe a >10% drop.

results.claim: Prompt-based fine-tuning with a manual prompt far exceeds standard few-shot fine-tuning on SST-2 and SNLI.
results.table: Table 3, row Prompt-based FT (man) vs Fine-tuning, columns SST-2 and SNLI

results.claim: T5-generated templates match manual ones on SST-2 and beat them on TREC where manual templates are hard to guess.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16, best single auto template chosen on Ddev, no demonstrations
results.table: Table 3, row Prompt-based FT (auto), column TREC 88.2 (2.0); row Prompt-based FT (man) TREC 84.8 (5.1)

results.claim: Auto label-word search is worse than manual on SNLI but better on TREC and MRPC; auto templates are the most consistent variant.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16; Auto L uses manual template; Auto T+L starts from manual label words, applies Auto T then Auto L
results.table: Table 5, rows Manual, Auto T, Auto L, Auto T + L; columns SST-2, SNLI, TREC, MRPC

results.claim: Selective demonstration sampling by SBERT beats uniform sampling on SNLI, TREC and MRPC.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16, manual prompts; top r=50% most similar per class
results.table: Table 7, rows Uniform sampling and + SBERT sel., column SNLI; TREC 85.6 vs 87.5; MRPC 70.9 vs 77.8; SST-2 92.3 vs 92.6
results.note: RoBERTa mean-pooled selection: SNLI 79.5, TREC 83.4, MRPC 76.6

results.claim: Ensembling auto templates beats PET's manual-prompt ensemble on RTE and MNLI.
results.setup: RoBERTa-large, K=16; PET uses 4 prompts for MNLI and 5 for RTE; equal-number comparison also reported
results.table: Table 4, rows PPET, Pours |Pours|=20 + demonstrations, column MNLI
results.note: Single manual prompt: 68.3 (MNLI), 69.1 (RTE); RTE PET 69.2, 20 auto 73.1, with demos 72.3 (demonstrations do not help on RTE here)

results.claim: A larger dev set helps both methods; with no dev set accuracy drops, e.g. prompt-based FT on SNLI.
results.table: Table A.1, Prompt-based FT, column SNLI rows No Ddev, |Ddev| = |Dtrain|, |Ddev| = 10|Dtrain|

results.claim: With 32 total examples LM-BFF nearly saturates on SST-2; on SNLI the gap over fine-tuning closes at about K=256.
results.unit: examples per class where SNLI curves converge
results.quote: until the two converge around K = 256.

results.claim: BERT-large also benefits from prompt-based fine-tuning but is much worse than RoBERTa-large; 2-segment embedding scheme is best with demonstrations.
results.setup: Manual prompts, K=16; BERT 2-seg + demos SNLI 61.3
results.table: Table D.1, BERT-large row Prompt-based FT and RoBERTa-large row Prompt-based FT, column SNLI

results.claim: Even with prompts, few-shot performance lags full-data fine-tuning, especially on harder tasks.

limits: Authors concede performance still lags fine-tuning with thousands of examples, especially on harder tasks, and results have high variance across splits.
Automatic prompt search is hard to expand or generalize from about 32 examples and still relies on manual templates (for label search) or manual label words (for template search).
LM-BFF favors tasks that are natural fill-in-the-blank problems, have short inputs and few output classes; structured prediction is left open.
SBERT used for demonstration selection was trained on SNLI and MNLI (acknowledged; RoBERTa mean-pooling control run).
SST-2 and SNLI were used for pilot experiments and development, so those two are not truly few-shot held out.
Only masked LMs of BERT/RoBERTa scale; no results on chat or decoder LLMs. The optimizer, schedule, warmup, precision and hardware are not stated.
